target_customer: Robotics labs and robot learning teams that need to judge whether a robot policy succeeded
problem: Evaluating robot learning runs is slow and manual, with people resetting and supervising robots during tests. Most Robotic builds a verification layer that scores each episode from the task and camera footage.
business_model: Research lab with a software product (Instance); pricing not public
product_category: Robot learning evaluation and verification software

founders.name: Claire Mao
founders.background_notes: Built software to simulate planetary atmospheres at NASA JPL and researched sustainable spaceflight propulsion at the MIT Media Lab, per the YC page.

founders.name: Lucy Cai
education: MIT, MEng in the Learning and Intelligent Systems lab
founders.background_notes: Friends with Mao since middle school, per the company site.

technical_complexity.rationale: Judging success of robot episodes from video requires reliable perception and task understanding across varied robots and tasks. Recent research on world models for policy evaluation shows the problem is open.

defensibility.rationale: Two founders and a new product with no disclosed customers or data. Large labs such as Runway publish similar evaluation work, so a head start is the main edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Runway published robot policy evaluation research and 1X uses a world model to score policies, so well-resourced players are near the wedge. No acquisition or copying outcome is known yet.

market_need_then: Robot learning teams spend manual effort supervising and resetting robots during evaluation. Research papers in 2026 on world models for policy evaluation show active demand for cheaper evaluation.

branding.domain_note: Uses mostrobotic.com, an exact match of the name.

identity.visual_style: Minimal site with lowercase text and a terse 'most robotic.' header
identity.voice_and_tone: Casual, playful and understated, with a personal friendship origin story

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive playful name and tone, but the company is weeks old with no press about the brand or community. Dealroom lists the legal entity as Instance Labs and the product as Instance, so name and product differ.

outcome_analysis: Most Robotic is a Summer 2026 company with two MIT founders who have NASA JPL, SpaceX and AWS experience. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found in a search. There is too little history to explain an outcome; the open questions are customer traction and whether larger labs absorb robot evaluation.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125k seed round, seen only on a partially locked aggregator page, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. No dated competitor sources near the June 2026 batch were found; Runway research is undated in the search result, so the list is empty. Dealroom says Instance Labs is the entity and Instance the product.
